false_positives.evidence: const stripeSecretKey = 'sk_live_FAKE…' is assigned directly in source and exposed through paymentClient().
false_positives.fix: Load the key at runtime from an environment variable or secret manager, remove it from source, and rotate it if it was ever valid.
false_positives.title: Hard-coded Stripe live-style secret key
false_positives.why: A credential-format value is committed in application source; anyone with repository access can use it, and it persists in git history. The value looks like a placeholder, so confirm whether it is real; the pattern is still unsafe.

false_positives.evidence: db.query(`SELECT * FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%${term}%'`) concatenates req.query.q into the SQL text.
false_positives.fix: Use a placeholder and pass the value separately: db.query('SELECT * FROM products WHERE name LIKE ?', [`%${term}%`]).
false_positives.title: SQL injection via string-interpolated search term

trace.note: interpolated into SQL passed to db.query with no params

false_positives.why: An attacker can break out of the LIKE literal and alter the query, reading or modifying arbitrary data. The db module here is a stub, so the real driver's behavior is unverified.

false_positives.evidence: req.query.file is used in uploads/${name} and out/${name}.png with no resolved-path containment check.
false_positives.fix: Accept only a basename matching a strict pattern, resolve both paths and verify they stay inside uploads/ and out/ before use.
false_positives.title: Path traversal in image conversion file parameter

trace.note: used as input and output file path by the convert command

false_positives.why: Values such as ../ segments let an attacker read files outside uploads/ as conversion input and write the output outside out/.

false_positives.evidence:
const name = String(req.query.file)
exec(`convert uploads/${name} out/${name}.png`, ...)
false_positives.fix: Accept only a basename matching a strict pattern, resolve it against the uploads directory and confirm the result stays inside it, and use a server-generated output name.
false_positives.title: Path traversal in image conversion file name

trace.note: concatenated into input and output paths of the convert binary

false_positives.why: name is used as a path under uploads/ and out/ with no resolve-plus-prefix containment check, so ../ sequences let a caller read an arbitrary file as conversion input and write a .png file outside out/. This is separate from the shell injection in the same line.

false_positives.evidence: memosDAO.insert(req.body.memo, ...) stores raw text; res.render("memos", { memosList: docs }); swig.setDefaults({ autoescape: false }) in server.js:135-137
false_positives.fix: Re-enable swig autoescaping (remove autoescape: false) and encode memo output for HTML context.
false_positives.title: Stored XSS: shared memos rendered with autoescape disabled

trace.note: req.body.memo stored via MemosDAO.insert with no sanitization
memo saved as-is; read back by getAllMemos
rendered into the memos template; autoescape disabled globally at server.js:137

false_positives.why: Memos are stored unmodified and shown to every user. With swig autoescape off, a memo containing script runs in other users' sessions, including admins. The view file is not in the repository, so the exact output expression could not be inspected.

false_positives.evidence: res.writeHead(200, { "Content-Type": "text/html" }); ... res.write(body);
false_positives.fix: Remove the client-chosen URL (see SEC-0006) and render fetched data through an escaping template, or serve it as text/plain.
false_positives.title: Reflected XSS: remote response written as text/html from /research
false_positives.why: The body fetched from an attacker-chosen URL is sent unescaped as HTML on the application's origin, so a link to /research?url=<attacker>&symbol=... runs attacker script in a logged-in victim's session.

false_positives.evidence: handleLoginRequest -> userDAO.validateLogin(userName, password, ...) with no rate limiter or failure counter; none registered in server.js
false_positives.fix: Add per-account and per-IP rate limiting (e.g. express-rate-limit) with temporary lockout, and return one generic login error.
false_positives.title: No attempt limit or lockout on login

trace.note: credential check runs on every request with no throttling

false_positives.why: An attacker can guess passwords at unlimited speed. Distinct 'Invalid username' / 'Invalid password' responses make valid accounts easy to find, and passwords are limited to 20 characters.

false_positives.evidence: res.status(500); res.render("error-template", { error: err });
false_positives.fix: Render a generic message to the client and keep details in server logs only.
false_positives.title: Raw error object passed to the error template

trace.note: err from any handler, including database errors
err given to the client-facing template

false_positives.why: The full error object (message, and stack if the template prints it) goes to the client, which can disclose database errors and file paths. The template is not in the repository, so what it prints is unverified.

false_positives.evidence: handleLoginRequest validates credentials with no throttling, lockout or rate-limiting middleware anywhere in the app.
false_positives.fix: Add per-account and per-IP rate limiting with backoff or lockout to POST /login.
false_positives.title: No attempt limit on login
false_positives.why: Attackers can brute-force passwords without limit; plaintext, short (max 20 char) passwords and distinct invalid-user/invalid-password messages make it easier.

false_positives.evidence: needle response body is written with res.write() under Content-Type text/html.
false_positives.fix: Do not relay remote HTML; return parsed data through an escaping template or Content-Type text/plain.
false_positives.title: Remote response body written unencoded into HTML response
false_positives.why: A crafted link to /research with an attacker-controlled url returns attacker HTML/script from the application's origin, enabling session-context script execution.

false_positives.evidence: res.render('error-template', { error: err }) passes the full error (message and stack).
false_positives.fix: Render a generic message and keep details in server logs only.
false_positives.title: Raw error object passed to client error template
false_positives.why: If the template prints the error, clients see stack traces and internal paths. The template is not in the repository, so rendering was not confirmed.

false_positives.evidence: ssn, dob, bankAcc and bankRouting are written as plain fields via $set; cryptoKey in config is never used.
false_positives.fix: Encrypt these fields with authenticated encryption (e.g. AES-256-GCM) and keys from a secret manager.
false_positives.title: Sensitive personal and bank data stored unencrypted
false_positives.why: Database or backup exposure reveals government IDs and bank details in clear text.

false_positives.evidence: "bcrypt-nodejs": "0.0.3"; the package is marked deprecated on npm in favor of bcrypt.
false_positives.fix: Replace with bcrypt or argon2.
false_positives.title: bcrypt-nodejs is deprecated
false_positives.why: Unmaintained password-hashing dependency receives no security fixes.

false_positives.title: Hard-coded ZAP API key in development config

false_positives.evidence: app.get("/benefits", isLoggedIn, ...); app.post("/benefits", isLoggedIn, ...); isAdmin is defined but never applied
false_positives.fix: Add the existing isAdmin middleware to both routes, and project only the fields the view needs (exclude password, ssn, bank fields).
false_positives.title: Benefits routes lack admin authorization and expose full user documents

trace.note: updateBenefits writes the body userId and date with no role check

false_positives.why: BR-1 allows only admins to view or change benefit start dates, but both routes need only a session. Any employee can change anyone's start date. The view also receives full user documents (plaintext password, SSN, bank details) from getAllNonAdminUsers, which the context describes as exposed to non-admins.

false_positives.evidence: memosDAO.insert(req.body.memo, ...) then render("memos", { memosList: docs }); swig.setDefaults({ autoescape: false })
false_positives.fix: Enable swig autoescape (remove autoescape: false) and encode memo output; render markdown only through a sanitising library.
false_positives.title: Stored XSS through memos with swig autoescape disabled
false_positives.why: Memo text is stored unmodified and shown to every user, and template autoescaping is off. A memo containing a script runs in each reader's browser, including admins. The view is out of scope, so the sink is inferred from the autoescape setting.

false_positives.evidence: handleLoginRequest calls userDAO.validateLogin with no rate limit, lockout or delay
false_positives.fix: Add per-account and per-IP rate limiting or lockout, and return one generic message for both failure cases.
false_positives.title: No brute-force protection on login

trace.note: each attempt is a plain lookup and compare

false_positives.why: An unauthenticated attacker can guess passwords without limit. The distinct messages "Invalid username" and "Invalid password" also confirm valid user names, which speeds up guessing.

false_positives.evidence: res.writeHead(200, {"Content-Type": "text/html"}); ... res.write(body);
false_positives.fix: Fix the upstream URL (see SEC-0005) and encode or parse the response; return JSON or text/plain, never raw remote HTML.
false_positives.title: Reflected XSS: /research writes fetched body as text/html
false_positives.why: The body fetched from an attacker-chosen URL is served unmodified as HTML from the app's origin. A crafted /research link that points at an attacker page runs script in the victim's session.

false_positives.evidence: routes(app, db) is registered with no helmet or header middleware; helmet and dont-sniff-mimetype are in package.json but not used
false_positives.fix: Add helmet() before the routes, set a CSP, and disable X-Powered-By.
false_positives.title: Security headers middleware absent (helmet unused)
false_positives.why: Responses carry no CSP, X-Frame-Options, nosniff or HSTS, and Express sends X-Powered-By. This weakens defence against clickjacking and against the XSS issues above.

false_positives.evidence: bcrypt-nodejs 0.0.3, marked 0.3.5 (pinned), needle 2.2.4 (pinned), node-esapi 0.0.1, swig ^1.4.2, mongodb ^2.1.18
false_positives.fix: Run npm audit, upgrade marked, needle and mongodb, and replace swig, bcrypt-nodejs and node-esapi with maintained libraries.
false_positives.title: Outdated and unmaintained dependencies
false_positives.why: These are very old or abandoned releases with no maintenance, and marked and needle process untrusted input. Advisories are likely for the pinned versions. I could not run npm audit, so none are confirmed here.
